notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because I never managed to read any of the source pages.

I sent one request for six pages: Enduring Word's Jeremiah 22, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, Precept Austin's Jeremiah 22 page, and the NET Bible notes. The requests went out, but my script failed while reading the replies, so I never saw what any page said. After that the tool stopped letting me run anything more in this turn, so I couldn't fix the script, try again or search other sites.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from memory. That rules out notes based on what I already know about these commentaries, and invented URLs or summaries would be worse than nothing.

If you ask again in a new message, I can:
1. Retry those six pages and handle the replies properly.
2. Add the other traditions you listed: Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God or Grace to You, Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org), and Catholic and Orthodox readings (newadvent.org, catholic.com). For the Catholic and Orthodox side, the Coniah curse in v. 30 and how it squares with Jesus's family line is a likely topic.
3. Write the notes verse by verse ("v. 4: …"), with a URL after each point and nothing included that I didn't find.
